\section{Gaussian Space --- Input Moments}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.InputMoments
\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Input Moments: Introduction}
Standard Gaussian variables and centered random signs satisfy the moment conditions used in fourth-order invariance.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Input Moments: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Fourth moment of a standard Gaussian]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_fourth_standardGaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{6}
If $X$ has the standard Gaussian probability measure on $\mathbb R$, then $\mathbb
E[X^4]=3$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Vanishing third Gaussian moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_third_standardGaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
If $Z$ has the standard Gaussian probability measure on $\mathbb R$, then $\int
z^3\,d\gamma(z)=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Second moment of a standard Gaussian]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_second_standardGaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{3}
If $Z$ has the standard Gaussian probability measure on $\mathbb R$, then $\int
z^2\,d\gamma(z)=1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian invariance input moments]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasInvarianceMoments_standardGaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_fourth_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_second_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_third_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p248-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p251-b003
}
\difficulty{4}
A standard real Gaussian random variable satisfies the invariance moment conditions: it has finite fourth absolute moment, its first three moments are $0,1,0$, and its fourth moment is at most $9$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Invariance moments for a sign-valued variable]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasInvarianceMoments_of_sq_eq_one}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space and let $X\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be
measurable up to a null set. Suppose $\int X\,d\mu=0$ and $X(\omega)^2=1$ for every
$\omega\in\Omega$. Then $X$ satisfies the invariance moment conditions: it is
$9$-reasonable, has second moment one, and has third moment zero.
\end{lemma}

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Input Moments: Further results}

\begin{lemma}[Invariance moments of a product coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasInvarianceMoments_pi_coordinate}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasInvarianceMoments_pi_coordinate}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments.identDistrib}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set, and for each $i\in I$ let $(A_i,\mu_i)$ be a probability space.
Suppose each function $X_i\colon A_i\to\mathbb R$ is measurable and satisfies the
invariance moment conditions under $\mu_i$. Then, for every chosen coordinate $i\in I$,
the function on $\prod_{j\in I}A_j$ given by $x\mapsto X_i(x_i)$ satisfies the
invariance moment conditions under the product measure $\bigotimes_{j\in I}\mu_j$.
\end{lemma}

  {BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasInvarianceMoments_pi_coordinate}
  {context}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p207-b002,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p207-b005}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$ and every coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the coordinate
function $z\mapsto z_i$ on $\mathbb R^n$, under product standard Gaussian measure,
satisfies the invariance moment conditions: it is $9$-reasonable, has mean zero, second
moment one, and third moment zero.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$ and coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, give the Boolean cube
$\{0,1\}^n$ the product of uniform probability measures on its coordinates. The function
that maps a point to the sign of its $i$th bit, with false encoded as $1$ and true as
$-1$, satisfies the invariance moment conditions.
\end{lemma}
